messages:
devon: Quick thought: instead of a fixed 'cooldown window' I'm proposing 'adaptive hysteresis' for autofallback. It'd consider recent fallback rate and a moving median latency to decide whether to suppress repeated fallbacks. Thoughts? :brain:

ana: Love the name. We've had noisy flip-flops on some routes when upstream GC hits for ~20s. Hysteresis might smooth that.

mike: How would we compute it cheaply in runtime? Can't make a heavy DB call per request.

devon: Keep it in-memory per routing shard. Maintain a sliding count and EWMA latency per route. Simple rule: if fallback_rate_last_30s > R_thresh AND latency_delta > L_thresh => suppress new fallbacks for hysteresis_period = base * (1 + alpha * oscillation_score).

riley: Can we express policy as a small rule set so ops can tweak it without deploys? Example proto: 
```yaml
fallback_policy_v2:
  mode: adaptive_hysteresis
  base_suppress: 8
  window_s: 30
  r_thresh: 0.1 # fraction of requests that fell back in window
  l_thresh_ms: 200
  alpha: 3.0 # multiplier for oscillation_score
  oscillation_metric: consecutive_fallback_spikes
  tier_overrides:
    dedicated:
      base_suppress: 4
    hosted_free:
      base_suppress: 12
  telemetry_sample_keys: [route, tenant_id, model_variant]
  operator_controls: {allow_override: true, max_override_mins: 60}
```

ana: That looks good. Two asks: 1) limit memory growth by capping number of tracked routes per shard, evict LRU; 2) surface oscillation_score in logs.

mike: Telemetry list: event=fallback_decision, route, tenant_tier, reason_code (timeout/oom/error), ewma_latency_before, ewma_latency_after, fallback_fraction, oscillation_score, decision (suppress/execute), trace_id. Make sampled traces include kv_cache_hit boolean.

jess: Console UX: show an inline badge on rollout rows: 'Hysteresis active' with tooltip -> "Adaptive suppression in effect (Xs left)". Clicking should open a mini-timeline with last 50 fallback events and their decision. Include a small replay button to fetch trace samples.

riley: For operator override flow: POST /console/v1/routes/{route}/fallback-override {duration_mins, reason, approver}. Must append an audit entry and show in timeline. Override should be rate-limited.

devon: Agreed. Audit entry format proposal (compact): 
``n[1829012345] route=payments charge, action=override_start, by=jess, dur_mins=15, reason='testing'
``nMake sure we also log a structured event to the audit stream for compliance.

ana: Edge: what happens if the fallback target itself returns 500s? We should detect fallback_failure_rate and after N attempts flip to degrade_mode (serve cached stub) and kick an incident. Proposed: fallback_failure_count >= 3 in 2m -> degrade_mode=set('stub'), page oncall.

mike: Rollout plan: feature-flag behind 0.5% of routes for 24h, escalate to 5% if no regressions, then 25% -> 100%. Monitoring thresholds: >2x error-rate, >1.3x p95 latency, >10% increase in fallback_count per route -> auto rollback. We'll need alerting hooks.

riley: For cohort sampling, we should bias toward high-traffic routes to validate oscillation handling under load, but include random low-traffic routes to catch regressions.

jess: UI telemetry: keep 'replay last N events' accessible only to SRE+ops roles. Also require a short reason when overriding. Modal copy: "Temporarily disable adaptive suppression for route X for Y minutes. This increases risk of oscillation. Provide reason to continue."

devon: Implementation sketch: runtime keeps a small ring buffer per route of (ts, decision, reason_code, ewma_before, ewma_after). A periodic flusher writes sampled entries to TSDB and audit stream. Sample retention TTL=30d.

mike: Add a retention TTL config and PII scrub policy on traces. Default TTL=30d, scrub_inputs=true for hosted_free tenants.

ops-bot: Reminder: any operator action (override/degrade_ack) must create an audit event and increment operator_action_metric.

riley: One more: provide a debug 'peek' API that returns the in-memory EWMA & counters for a route (GET /runtime/v1/routes/{route}/debug). Auth gated. Useful for on-call triage.

ana: Love that. Saves a ton of back-and-forth on PagerDuty nights.

devon: I'm going to draft the RFC with this proto + rollout + alerts. Volunteers for paired reviews?

ana: I'll own the metrics panel and thresholds with observability.

jess: I'll prototype the console badge and modal tomorrow AM.

mike: I'll help wire runtime endpoints + retention hooks.

deploy-bot: scheduled: feature-flag adaptive-hysteresis-autofallback -> staging at 2024-11-05T09:00Z

devon: Thanks all. I'll post RFC link once created. If anyone has quick counterexamples where hysteresis could make things worse, drop them here.

jess: One quick: long-tail bursty traffic might suppress fallbacks too aggressively; let's ensure there's a hard cap so suppression can't exceed 5 minutes by default.

devon: Noted. Add max_suppress_s: 300 to proto.

mike: Also consider a safety 'force_fallback' path for critical routes if operator deems fallback preferable to degraded stub.

riley: Good call. We'll add force_fallback API and require RBAC.

ana: Ok looping in observability after RFC.

devon: Cool. RFC incoming. :thumbsup:
